free_tier.stated: CloudLab gives free bare-metal nodes with no allocation accounting at all: "Registering doesn't cost anything, it's simply for accountability. We just ask that if you're going to use CloudLab for anything other than light use, you tell us a bit more about who you are." The Utah cluster alone is 9,336 cores across 1,000-plus nodes, including 28 nodes of 32-core AMD EPYC 7452 with 100Gb Ethernet and 36 nodes of 24-core EPYC 7402P with 25/100Gb links.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The absence of a quota is the unusual part and it is what makes CloudLab usable for a long-running measurement rather than a benchmark: a project can hold nodes for days provided the profile reserves them, which is the shape a network or storage experiment needs and which no credit-based programme provides.

limits.value: Creating a project requires being "faculty, senior research staff, or in some other senior position" and passes a staff review that takes a few days; joining one requires the leader's approval, so an unaffiliated person cannot obtain nodes on their own.
